_comment: Known gaps shown by jarvis-status. Edited here, not in the script, so closing a gap is a data change rather than a code change. A gap NEVER makes the overall status FAIL -- it is a documented limitation, not a fault.

gaps.note: Detector and audio pipeline are alive, but intentional-user recall and ambient false-positive rate are not yet reliable. Evidence 2026-09-02: openWakeWord running, feed_errors=0, and a detector-origin wake was observed firing on its own at 13:32:20 (PEAK_RMS=130, no speech) -- so the engine fires. What it missed was a deliberate "Hey Jarvis" earlier the same session. This is calibration, not a dead engine. Cmd+Shift+J remains the reliable path. No threshold or model change has been made. 2026-09-09: still untouched. The adaptive silence threshold (NoiseFloorTracker) changed capture termination only, not wake detection.

Recovery from a clamshell sleep/wake cycle has still never been observed -- and 2026-09-09 measurement shows why: this machine does not sleep. `pmset -g custom` reports `sleep 0` for AC Power (and `displaysleep 0`), Amphetamine held PreventUserIdleSystemSleep for 21h40m, and `pmset -g log` reported `Total Sleep/Wakes since boot at 2026-09-08 19:38:41 +0900 :0` -- zero cycles since the reboot that started this runtime. The user works clamshell on AC through a DisplayLink dock, so idle sleep never fires. This gap was previously ranked low as 'never observed'; it was then briefly ranked HIGH on the assumption that clamshell operation exercises it, which was wrong -- clamshell operation on AC actively prevents it. Re-ranked LOW. It becomes reachable only if the machine runs on battery and sleeps, or if the power configuration changes. jarvis-status now surfaces this precondition in the Power row so the next attempt does not re-derive it.

A turn started while the startup warm is still retrying is unmeasured. Argued safe -- Ollama serves one runner per model -- but not observed. 2026-09-09: the real login/warm validation had a 35s readiness wait plus model load to 20:56, which would have been the window, but the turn was deliberately held until warm completed so the latency measurement stayed clean. Still unobserved.
